facts.claim: A person engaged in a profession, trade, calling, or employment and falling under a class in Schedule I is liable to pay tax at the rate specified in the schedule.
facts.subject: person_in_profession_or_trade
facts.evidence: Every person engaged in any profession, trade, calling or employment and falling under one or the other of the classes mentioned in column 2 of Schedule. 1 shall he liable to pay to the State Government the tax at the rate mentioned against the class of such person in column 3 of the said Schedule.

facts.claim: The tax payable by a person in a year shall not exceed two thousand and five hundred rupees.
facts.subject: tax_payable
facts.evidence: Provided that the tax so payable in respect of any one person shall not exceed two thousand and five hundred rupees in any year :

facts.claim: The State Government may specify additional classes of persons to whom entry 10 in Schedule I applies, and the tax rate for these persons shall not exceed two thousand rupees per year.
facts.subject: state_government
facts.evidence: Provided further that the State Government may, from time to time, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify the class of persons other than those mentioned in entries 1 to 9 in Schedule 1 to whom entry 10 in that Schedule shall apply and the rate (not exceeding two thousand rupees every year) at which the tax shall be payable by the class of persons so specified.

facts.claim: If a person falls under more than one entry in Schedule I, they must pay tax under the entry with the highest tax rate.
facts.subject: person_in_multiple_entries
facts.evidence: Where a person falls under more than one entry in Schedule-1, he shall be liable to pay the 2[Designated Authority] the tax under such one of these entries where the rate of tax specified is the highest.

facts.claim: A person falling under entries 2 to 10 in Schedule I is liable to pay tax for the year, regardless of whether they were engaged in the profession, trade, calling, or employment for the whole year or part thereof.
facts.subject: person_in_entries_2_to_10
facts.evidence: A person falling under any of the entries 2 to 10 in Schedule-1 shall be liable to pay the tax for the year irrespective of whether he is engaged in the profession, trade calling or employment during the whole of such year or any part thereof

facts.claim: If a person is liable to pay tax to more than one Designated Authority, they must pay the tax to the one with the highest tax liability.
facts.subject: person_with_multiple_authorities
facts.evidence: Where a person falling under any of the entries in Schedule I is liable to pay the tax to more than one Designated Authority, he shall pay the tax to the Designated Authority where the tax liability is highest:

facts.claim: If a person provides a certificate that tax has been paid to the Designated Authority with the highest liability, no other Designated Authority may levy the tax.
facts.subject: person_with_certificate
facts.evidence: Provided that where a person produces a certificate to the effect that the tax has been paid by him to the Designated Authority where the liability of tax is highest, the tax shall not be levied by any other Designated Authority.

facts.claim: The Antyeshti Aid Scheme provides financial assistance of ₹5000 to the legal heir of a registered construction worker who dies while their membership is active.
facts.subject: antyeshti_aid_scheme
facts.evidence: બાંધકામ વ્યવસાયમાં રોકાયેલ અને નોંધાયેલ લાભાર્થી શ્રમયોગીનું ચાલુ મેમ્બરશીપ દરમિયાન મૃત્યુ થાય તો મૃત્યુ પામનારના ઉત્તરાધિકારીને અંત્યેષ્ઠિ સહાય યોજના હેઠળ રૂ.૫૦૦૦/- નાંણાકિય સહાય આપવાની જોગવાઈ આ યોજનામાં કરવામાં આવેલ છે.

facts.claim: An application form (in the given format) is required to apply for the Antyeshti Aid Scheme.
facts.subject: antyeshti_aid_scheme
facts.evidence: અરજી પત્રક(નમૂનામાં)

facts.claim: A death certificate is required to apply for the Antyeshti Aid Scheme.
facts.subject: antyeshti_aid_scheme
facts.evidence: મરણ અંગેનું પ્રમાણપત્ર

facts.claim: A photocopy of the beneficiary's identity card is required to apply for the Antyeshti Aid Scheme.
facts.subject: antyeshti_aid_scheme

facts.claim: The heir must submit the application to the Project Manager of the Gujarat Housing and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board in the respective district.
facts.subject: antyeshti_aid_scheme

facts.claim: Eligible mothers under the BPL will receive Rs. 500 for medical treatment and food during childbirth.
facts.subject: janani_suraksha_scheme
facts.evidence: જનની સુરક્ષા યોજનામાં અનુસુચિત જાતિ, અનુસુચિત જન જાતિના તમામ અન્‍ય માટે ગરીબી રેખાથી નીચે જીવતા કુટુંબની પ્રસુતા માતાઓને પ્રસુતિ સમયે દવા સારવાર અને ખોરાક માટે તમારા ગામના સ્‍થાનિક નર્સબેન પાસેથી રૂ.૫૦૦/- અંકે રૂપિયા પાંચસો પુરા ચુકવવામાં આવશે.

facts.claim: Eligible mothers must be 19 years of age or older.
facts.subject: janani_suraksha_scheme
facts.evidence: ૧૯ વર્ષ કે તેથી વયની હોય.

facts.claim: The scheme is applicable only for up to two live births.
facts.subject: janani_suraksha_scheme
facts.evidence: બે જીવીત જન્‍મો સુધી જ લાગુ પડશે.

facts.claim: The Antyesthi Aid Scheme provides financial assistance of ₹5000 to the legal heir of a registered construction worker who dies while their membership is active.

facts.evidence: બાંધકામ વ્યવસાયમાં રોકાયેલ અને નોંધાયેલ લાભાર્થી શ્રમયોગીનું ચાલુ મેમ્બરશીપ દરમિયાન મૃત્યુ થાય તો મૃત્યુ પામનારના ઉત્તરાધિકારીને અંત્યેષ્ઠિ સહાય યોજના હેઠળ રૂ.૫૦૦૦/- નાંણાકિય સહાય આપવાની જોગવાઈ આ યોજનામાં કરવામાં આવેલ છે.

facts.claim: AB PM-JAY provides a health cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to over 15 crores poor and vulnerable families.
facts.subject: ab_pm_jay
facts.evidence: AB PM-JAY is the largest health assurance scheme in the world, launched on 23rd September 2018 in Ranchi, Jharkhand and is aimed at providing a health cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to over 15 crores poor and vulnerable families.

facts.claim: AB PM-JAY covers 15.14 crore eligible families as of 31st March 2025.
facts.subject: ab_pm_jay
facts.evidence: As of 31st March 2025, AB PM-JAY covers 15.14 crore eligible families and an additional 8 crore+ families under state schemes, reinforcing the Government’s commitment to equitable healthcare for all and also accelerated India’s progress towards the achievement of Universal Health Coverage and Sustainable Development Goal 3.

facts.claim: AB PM-JAY is fully funded by the government, with costs shared between central and state governments in the ratio of 60:40 for most states.
facts.subject: ab_pm_jay

detail.exception_states: North-Eastern States and Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand

facts.evidence: The AB PM-JAY scheme is fully funded by the government, and costs are shared between central and state governments in the ratio of 60:40, for states (other than North-Eastern States and Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand) and Union Territories (UTs) with legislature. In these states, the ratio is 90:10 and in UTs without legislatures, the Central Government may provide up to 100% on a case-to-case basis.

facts.subject: isa_written_notice
facts.evidence: Whenever any such complain comes to the notice of ISA for the first time, ISA will issue a notice in written to the respective hospital to return the said amount to the respective beneficiary.

facts.claim: The hospital must submit receipts to the ISA within 15 days after receiving the notice.

facts.evidence: The hospital will submit receipts against the same from the beneficiary to the ISA within 15 days.

facts.claim: If the hospital repeats the fraudulent activity, it will return the charged amount to the patient and an equal amount will be deducted as a penalty from the claim amount by the ISA.

facts.evidence:
